idiom_name: Nokogiri::XML::Builder logical page + Nokogiri::XSLT stylesheet per channel
implementation_notes: Stage one builds the logical page with Nokogiri's builder DSL, which yields a real XML document with no HTML decoration; stage two renders it with Nokogiri::XSLT(stylesheet).transform(doc) for a stylesheet-driven channel, or serialises the same document per channel (.to_xml, .to_html, a JSON encoder). Compile the stylesheet once at boot and keep the builder output free of presentation attributes. Ruby's web stacks reach the same shape through Action View, where the model and assigns are the logical page and a per-format template or handler renders each channel; the Nokogiri route is the one to take when the second stage should be a stylesheet rather than Ruby code.
code_sketch:
page = Nokogiri::XML::Builder.new do |xml|        # stage 1: logical page
  xml.invoice(total: "42.00") { xml.customer "ACME" }
end

stylesheet = Nokogiri::XSLT(File.read("invoice-html.xsl"))  # compiled once
html = stylesheet.transform(page.doc)                          # stage 2: HTML channel
# text or feed channels: page.doc.to_xml / a serializer over the same data
pitfalls: Nokogiri's documentation warns that libxslt cannot safely process untrusted stylesheets - external entities are resolved and file plus network access are unrestricted - so never load a stylesheet from user input.
Builder tag names collide with Ruby methods: reserved words need the trailing underscore (xml.class_, xml.type_), otherwise the builder raises or emits the wrong element.
Nokogiri::XSLT.register installs custom XSLT functions globally, so one request's handler is visible to every other renderer in the process.
